chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), said:
I asked him about the one in Ihram, can he buy the slave girl and sell? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram buy and sell slave girls?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibitions of Ihram do not extend to commercial transactions, specifically permitting the buying and selling of female slaves. This ruling underscores the distinction between ritual restrictions on personal conduct and the continuity of economic rights during the pilgrimage state, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding the scope of *Mahdurat*.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws, said,
‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam, ‘Can he buy the slave girl, and sell?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Barqiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who is in the state of Ihram; if he can buy and sell slave-girls. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so.”
